newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SEES FIRST OPEN-END FOREIGN SECURITIES FUND.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SEES FIRST OPEN-END FOREIGN SECURITIES FUND.

text.p: Hungary's Europool Investment Fund Management will start offering its Hunnia IV open-end securities investment fund on December 6, officials said on Wednesday.
"This will be the first open-end securities fund to offer Hungarians the possibility to invest abroad," Gyula Fater, Europool's general director, told a news conference.
He added that open-end funds have proved to be a big success in Hungary, presently managing some 60 billion forints ($370 million) of net assets, equal to four percent of all domestic savings.
Europool's share of the open-end fund market is 12.9 percent, Fater said.
London-based John Govett & Co Ltd will be the investment advisor for the fund.
"In our investment policy we will be opportunistic but in a risk-adverse manner," said Kevin Pakenham, general manager of John Govett.
The fund aims at a return above yields from German mark deposits but this is not guaranteed, he added.
Investors subscribed 135 million forints, 35 million forints more than the initial 100 million forints required to start the fund, Fater said.
Inter-Europa Bank will act as custodian and New York Broker Budapest, which also guaranteed the initial 100 million forints subscription, as sales manager.
